tasks.title: Lecture #2
tasks.instruction: Listen to part of a lecture in a United States history class.
tasks.transcript:
In the days before telephones, radio, and television, the only network of public communication that could reach farmers was the mail. But this wasn’t the mail as we know it today. At that time, in the early nineteenth century, mail delivery was uneven and widely scattered. In fact, many people living in rural areas got no mail at all. In the early decades of the century, mail carriers were privately employed – they did not work for the government. Many years later, when the government finally took charge of delivering mail, it was mostly in cities that mail got delivered to people’s homes. So farmers still had a problem – they had to go to a post office to collect their mail, which, by the way, wasn’t always nearby. Farmers’ requests to have mail brought to their homes were at first met with outrage. What could be more ridiculous, many urban residents asked, than paying government employees to travel miles across the countryside with an occasional letter? Nevertheless, farmers’ organizations succeeded in convincing the United States Congress that farmers needed mail delivery. Finally in 1891 rural free delivery, known as RFD, came into being.
In a sense, rural free delivery was the most important communications revolution in United States history. Rural Americans were not lifted out of the relatively isolated communities they lived in. Because of rural free delivery, there now ran a highway to the world from every farmer’s doorstep.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The economic impact of mail delivery on rural areas.
options.B: A comparison of urban and rural mail delivery.
options.D: The introduction of mail delivery in rural areas.

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：演讲者主要讨论什么？ 定位原文：In the days before telephones... the only network of public communication that could reach farmers was the mail. ... Finally in 1891 rural free delivery, known as RFD, came into being. ... Because of rural free delivery, there now ran a highway to the world from every farmer's doorstep. 选项分析： A. 邮件投递对农村地区的经济影响。演讲者提到RFD是重要的通信革命，让农民不再与世隔绝，但并未具体讨论其经济影响，因此A选项错误。 B. 城市和农村邮件投递的比较。演讲中确实提到了城市和农村投递的差异，但这是为了说明农村投递服务的缺失和最终引入的背景，并非讨论的主旨，因此B选项错误。 C. 城市的政府邮件投递。演讲提到政府最初只在城市投递邮件，但这只是背景信息，核心在于后来农村投递服务的建立，因此C选项错误。 D. 农村地区邮件投递的引入。演讲从早期农村没有邮件服务讲起，描述了农民面临的困境、他们的请求以及最终RFD的建立，整篇都在围绕农村邮件投递如何被引入而展开，因此D选项正确。

questions.stem: What is true of mail delivery in the early nineteenth century?

options.A: It was paid for by the United States Congress.
options.B: It was run by private companies.
options.C: It was regulated by the government.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：关于19世纪初的邮件投递，哪一项是正确的？ 定位原文：In the early decades of the century, mail carriers were privately employed – they did not work for the government. 选项分析： A. 它由美国国会支付。原文并未提及国会支付，后来国会是通过了RFD法案，而非支付早期投递，因此A选项错误。 B. 它由私营公司运营。原文明确指出当时的邮差是私人雇佣的，不为政府工作，因此B选项正确。 C. 它受政府监管。原文说邮差是私人雇佣，不受政府管辖，因此C选项错误。 D. 它主要面向农民。原文提到当时农村地区很多人根本收不到邮件，因此D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what problem did farmers face with early mail service?

options.A: Many post office locations were inconvenient.
options.C: The postal rates were too high.
options.D: There were not enough mail carriers to deliver mail.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：根据演讲者的说法，农民在早期邮件服务中面临什么问题？ 定位原文：So farmers still had a problem – they had to go to a post office to collect their mail, which, by the way, wasn't always nearby. 选项分析： A. 许多邮局的位置不方便。原文明确指出农民必须去邮局取邮件，而邮局并不总是在附近，这正是不方便的表现，因此A选项正确。 B. 糟糕的道路延误了邮件投递。原文并未提及道路状况，因此B选项错误。 C. 邮资太高。原文没有讨论邮资问题，因此C选项错误。 D. 没有足够的邮差投递邮件。原文提到政府在城市投递邮件，但在农村需要农民自取，问题在于投递方式而非邮差数量不足，因此D选项错误。

questions.stem: How did many city residents reach when farmers first requested mail delivery?

options.B: They thought it should have been done long before.
options.D: They thought it had to be accepted despite its cost.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：当农民首次要求邮件投递时，许多城市居民反应如何？ 定位原文：Farmers' requests to have mail brought to their homes were at first met with outrage. What could be more ridiculous, many urban residents asked, than paying government employees to travel miles across the countryside with an occasional letter? 选项分析： A. 他们对此漠不关心。城市居民的反应是愤慨（outrage），而非漠不关心，因此A选项错误。 B. 他们认为早就该这样做了。这与城市居民反对的态度相反，因此B选项错误。 C. 他们认为这是不必要的。城市居民质问“还有什么比付钱给政府雇员带着偶尔一封信穿越乡村更荒谬的”，这表达了他们认为此举毫无必要、荒谬可笑的态度，因此C选项正确。 D. 他们认为尽管有成本，也必须接受。城市居民的态度是反对，并不认为应该接受，因此D选项错误。
